guidebook.intro: Talking about kings and kingdoms in Swahili: the words you need for the Kabaka of Buganda, and for the coast’s favourite trickster, Abunuwasi.

tips.title: Ufalme, ikulu: abstract and place nouns
body: **u-** makes a word for a quality or a realm: **mfalme** (king) gives **ufalme** (kingdom). Its adjectives take **w-**: **ufalme wa Buganda** (the kingdom of Buganda).
**ikulu** (palace) and **bunge** (parliament) are everyday words in Kenya and Tanzania too, for the State House and the national parliament.

tips.title: hu-: things that always happen
body: **hu-** in front of a verb, with no person prefix, says something happens as a rule: **bunge hukaa Bulange** (parliament sits at Bulange).

culture.title: Abunuwasi
body: Abunuwasi (from the Arabic poet Abu Nuwas) is the clever hero of Swahili coastal tales. He outwits sultans and kings with a straight face, and every story ends with the king laughing, or paying.
